q: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company is planning a hybrid identity solution and wants to minimize on-premises footprint while still synchronizing user accounts, groups, and password hashes to Microsoft Entra ID. Which synchronization method should you recommend?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra Connect with full synchronization
B. Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
C. Microsoft Entra Connect with pass-through authentication only
D. Microsoft Identity Manager (MIM)
explain: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended lightweight agent-based solution that runs on multiple servers, has a smaller on-premises footprint, and supports synchronizing users, groups, and password hashes. Entra Connect is the older, heavier solution that requires more infrastructure. Pass-through authentication does not synchronize password hashes, and MIM is legacy and not the strategic direction.

q: Contoso uses Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The on-premises Active Directory contains a security group named SG-Exec that should be synchronized to Entra ID as a Microsoft 365 Group with dynamic membership rules applied in the cloud. What must be done to achieve this?
choices: A. Convert the group to a distribution group before synchronization
B. Enable group writeback and create the dynamic group in Entra ID
C. Synchronize the security group and then change its group type in Entra ID
D. Use Entra Cloud Sync instead of Entra Connect
explain: Security groups synchronized from on-premises cannot be directly converted to Microsoft 365 Groups with dynamic membership in Entra ID. The recommended approach is to enable group writeback and create a new dynamic Microsoft 365 Group in the cloud. Changing group type after sync is not supported, and switching sync tools does not solve the group type limitation.

q: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Connect Cloud Sync? (Choose all that apply, but select the best single answer that represents the most complete option)
choices: A. Users and security groups only
B. Users, groups, and devices
C. Users, groups, password hashes, and public folder contacts
D. Users, groups, and password hashes
explain: Entra Cloud Sync supports synchronizing users, groups (security and Microsoft 365), and password hashes. It does not support device synchronization or public folder contacts (those require full Entra Connect). Option D is the most accurate single choice among the provided options.

q: You need to create a guest user account for a partner company that uses a non-Azure AD identity provider. The partner must be able to access a specific SharePoint Online site using their existing corporate credentials. What should you configure?
choices: A. Direct federation using SAML 2.0
B. Microsoft Entra B2B with email one-time passcode
C. Microsoft Entra B2B with Google federation
D. Self-service sign-up with custom workflow
explain: Direct federation (SAML/WS-Fed) allows the partner to use their own corporate identity provider for authentication, which matches the requirement. Email OTP is for organizations without an identity provider. Google federation is limited to Google accounts only. Self-service sign-up is for consumer scenarios, not corporate partners.

q: What is the default synchronization interval for password hash synchronization when using Microsoft Entra Connect?
choices: A. Every 2 minutes
B. Every 30 minutes
C. Every 2 hours
D. Every 24 hours
explain: Password hash synchronization with Entra Connect occurs every 30 minutes by default. The 2-minute interval applies to other attribute syncs in newer versions, but password hash sync remains on a 30-minute cycle. The 2-hour and 24-hour options are incorrect.

q: Your organization has a requirement to prevent all guest users from being able to enumerate the membership of any Microsoft 365 Group. Which setting in the Microsoft Entra admin center should you modify?
choices: A. External collaboration settings – Guest user access
B. External collaboration settings – Guest invite restrictions
C. Group settings – Restrict guest access to groups
D. User settings – Restrict access to the Entra admin portal
explain: The Group settings option 'Restrict guest access to groups' controls whether guests can see group membership. This is the specific control needed. External collaboration settings control invitation and user access levels but do not directly control group membership visibility. The other options are unrelated.

q: You are configuring Microsoft Entra Connect for a hybrid environment. The company wants to use Seamless Single Sign-On (SSO) and Password Hash Synchronization. Which two prerequisites must be met? (Choose two, but select the option that lists the correct pair)
choices: A. The server must be domain-joined and have direct internet access
B. Port 443 must be open outbound and the server must have line-of-sight to a writable domain controller
C. The forest functional level must be Windows Server 2012 or higher and the Entra Connect server must be joined to the domain
D. Azure AD Connect Health must be installed and the server must run Windows Server 2019
explain: For Seamless SSO and PHS, the forest functional level must be at least Windows Server 2012 and the Entra Connect server must be domain joined. Option B is partially correct but incomplete. Option A is incorrect because the server does not require direct internet access if a proxy is configured. Option D is not required.

q: A user object synchronized from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID has the attribute userType set to 'Member'. You want this user to be treated as a guest in Entra ID for licensing and Conditional Access purposes. What is the recommended way to achieve this?
choices: A. Change the userType attribute to 'Guest' in on-premises AD and wait for the next sync cycle
B. Use the Microsoft Graph API to update the userType property in Entra ID
C. Disable and re-enable the user account in Entra ID
D. Add the user to the 'Guests' security group
explain: For synchronized users, the userType attribute is authoritative from on-premises and cannot be changed directly in Entra ID. The recommended and supported method is to update the userType using Microsoft Graph API (or PowerShell) in the cloud. Changing it on-premises is not honored for this attribute. The other options do not change the userType property.

q: Which of the following is a key advantage of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync over Microsoft Entra Connect?
choices: A. It supports more object types including devices and contacts
B. It uses a lightweight multi-agent architecture with no single point of failure
C. It provides real-time synchronization instead of scheduled
D. It includes built-in group writeback capabilities without additional configuration
explain: Entra Cloud Sync uses multiple lightweight agents for high availability and has a much smaller on-premises footprint than the full Entra Connect synchronization service. It does not support more object types (actually supports fewer), is not real-time, and still requires configuration for group writeback.

q: You manage external identities for Fabrikam. Several vendors need to access internal applications using their own corporate identities from identity providers that support OpenID Connect. What feature should you configure in Microsoft Entra ID to meet this requirement with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra B2B direct federation
B. Microsoft Entra B2C custom policies
C. Self-service sign-up with identity providers
D. Microsoft Entra External Identities with SAML applications
explain: Microsoft Entra B2B direct federation supports both SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect identity providers, allowing users to sign in with their corporate credentials. This is the correct B2B feature for organizational partners. B2C is for consumer-facing applications, self-service sign-up is for email-based scenarios, and the SAML option is too narrow.

q: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to synchronize user accounts and groups from an on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID while minimizing the amount of data sent to the cloud. Which hybrid identity solution should you implement?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra Connect with full synchronization
B. Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
C. Microsoft Entra Connect with pass-through authentication only
D. Microsoft Entra Connect Health
explain: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended lightweight solution that uses a cloud-based provisioning agent and sends significantly less data to the cloud compared to the full Entra Connect sync client. Option A uses the legacy heavier client, option C is an authentication method not a sync method, and option D is a monitoring tool.

q: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft Entra Connect?
choices: A. Users, groups, and devices
B. Users, groups, contacts, and devices
C. Users and security groups only
D. Users, distribution groups, and computer accounts only
explain: Entra Connect can synchronize users, groups (both security and distribution), contacts, and devices. Option A is missing contacts, option C is too restrictive, and option D incorrectly limits group types and includes computer accounts which are not directly synced as objects.

q: Contoso is planning a merger with Fabrikam. Fabrikam users need to access Contoso resources using their existing Fabrikam credentials without creating new accounts. What should you configure in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. A new Entra ID tenant for Fabrikam
B. Cross-tenant synchronization
C. B2B collaboration with external identities
D. Password hash synchronization between tenants
explain: B2B collaboration allows external users (Fabrikam) to use their own credentials to access Contoso resources through invitations or self-service sign-up. Cross-tenant sync is for internal employee synchronization between tenants, not guest access. Options A and D are not the correct approach for this scenario.

q: You need to create a group in Microsoft Entra ID that will be used to assign licenses to users in the Marketing department. The group must be dynamically updated when users change departments. Which group type and membership type should you configure?
choices: A. Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
B. Security group with dynamic user membership
C. Security group with assigned membership
D. Microsoft 365 group with dynamic device membership
explain: A security group with dynamic user membership uses membership rules based on user attributes (such as department) and can be used for license assignment. Microsoft 365 groups can also be dynamic but are primarily for collaboration. Device membership is not applicable for user licensing.

q: Which protocol and port combination is used by default for synchronization between Microsoft Entra Connect and Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. HTTPS over port 443
B. HTTP over port 80
C. LDAP over port 389
D. SMB over port 445
explain: Microsoft Entra Connect uses outbound HTTPS connections over port 443 to communicate with Entra ID. LDAP, HTTP, and SMB are not used for the synchronization service communication with the cloud.

q: Your organization has a requirement to allow users to sign in with their on-premises credentials without storing password hashes in the cloud. Which authentication method should be implemented with Microsoft Entra Connect?
choices: A. Password hash synchronization
B. Federation with AD FS
C. Pass-through authentication
D. Seamless single sign-on only
explain: Pass-through authentication validates passwords against on-premises Active Directory without storing hashes in the cloud. Password hash sync stores hashes, federation uses AD FS, and seamless SSO is a sign-in enhancement that works with either PHS or PTA.

q: You are configuring a new Entra ID tenant for a partner organization. You want to allow users from contoso.com to access your applications as guests. What must be configured in the External Identities section?
choices: A. Enable B2C user flows
B. Add contoso.com as an identity provider in B2B
C. Configure cross-tenant access settings to allow inbound access from contoso.com
D. Create a new conditional access policy for external users
explain: Cross-tenant access settings must be configured to allow inbound B2B access from specific tenants such as contoso.com. Adding as an identity provider is not required for standard B2B. B2C is for consumer identities, and conditional access is applied after the external user is allowed.

q: What is the maximum number of on-premises Active Directory forests that a single Microsoft Entra Connect server can synchronize to a single Microsoft Entra tenant?
choices: D. No limit
explain: A single Entra Connect server can synchronize up to 5 on-premises AD forests to one Entra tenant. Synchronization from more than 5 forests requires additional Connect servers or the use of Entra Cloud Sync.

q: Litware Inc. wants to create a dynamic security group that includes all users whose job title contains 'Manager' and who are located in the United States. Which membership rule syntax should be used?
choices: A. (user.jobTitle -contains "Manager") -and (user.country -eq "US")
B. (user.jobTitle equals "Manager") and (user.country equals "United States")
C. user.jobTitle -like "*Manager*" && user.usageLocation -eq "US"
D. (user.title contains "Manager") or (user.country -eq "US")
explain: The correct syntax uses the -contains and -eq operators with the proper attribute names (jobTitle and country). Option B uses incorrect operator names, option C uses usageLocation instead of country and incorrect operators, and option D uses 'or' instead of 'and' and the wrong attribute (title).

q: You have deployed Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync for a hybrid environment. After the initial sync cycle, you notice that several on-premises groups are missing in Entra ID. What is the most likely reason?
choices: A. The groups are distribution groups and were not selected in the sync scope
B. Cloud Sync does not support group synchronization
C. The groups have more than 500 members
D. The Entra Cloud Sync service account does not have Replicating Directory Changes permission
explain: The Cloud Sync service account requires the 'Replicating Directory Changes' permission on the on-premises domain to read group objects. Cloud Sync does support group synchronization (eliminating B), distribution groups are supported, and member count is not a limiting factor for visibility.

q: Your organization is planning to synchronize user accounts from an on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID. You need to choose a synchronization method that supports password hash synchronization, pass-through authentication, and seamless single sign-on while minimizing the number of servers required. Which solution should you recommend?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra Connect with password hash synchronization
B. Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
C. Microsoft Entra Connect with pass-through authentication
D. Microsoft Entra Connect cloud provisioning
explain: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended modern solution as it is a lightweight agent-based service that supports password hash sync, PTA, and SSO with significantly lower infrastructure requirements than the legacy Entra Connect sync client. Option A and C refer to the older Entra Connect sync client which requires more servers and maintenance. Option D is not a valid product name.

q: You are configuring group writeback from Microsoft Entra ID to an on-premises Active Directory. Which type of group can be successfully written back using Entra Connect?
choices: A. Microsoft 365 groups
B. Security groups with dynamic membership
C. Security groups with assigned membership
D. All of the above
explain: Only security groups that have assigned membership can be written back to on-premises AD. Microsoft 365 groups and dynamic groups are cloud-only and cannot be written back. This limitation is important when planning group management in hybrid environments.

q: Contoso is using Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The HR department has asked that all users with the job title 'Contractor' be automatically added to a specific security group in Microsoft Entra ID. What is the best way to achieve this requirement?
choices: A. Create a dynamic user group using the jobTitle attribute
B. Use Entra Connect to create an OU filter for contractors
C. Configure group writeback rules in Entra Connect
D. Manually add contractors to the group on a weekly basis
explain: Dynamic user groups in Microsoft Entra ID can automatically add or remove members based on attributes such as jobTitle. This is the most efficient method. Entra Connect OU filtering controls which objects are synchronized but does not create dynamic group membership in the cloud. Group writeback works in the opposite direction.

q: Which of the following is a valid source of authority for a user account that has been synchronized from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Connect?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra ID
B. On-premises Active Directory
C. Both simultaneously
D. Neither - the account is orphaned
explain: When an object is synchronized from on-premises AD using Entra Connect, the source of authority remains on-premises. Most attributes can only be changed in the on-premises AD and then synchronized to the cloud. This is a core concept of hybrid identity with Entra Connect.

q: You need to allow users from a partner organization using their own Azure AD tenant to access your company's SaaS application registered in Microsoft Entra ID. What should you configure?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
B. Microsoft Entra B2C
C. Microsoft Entra Domain Services
D. Self-service password reset
explain: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration is designed for inviting and managing external users from other organizations (including other Azure AD tenants) to access your resources. B2C is for consumer-facing applications with local accounts or social identity providers. Domain Services is for managed domain services.

q: Your company is migrating from Microsoft Entra Connect to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. What is one key advantage of Cloud Sync over the traditional Entra Connect sync client?
choices: A. It supports more than 500,000 objects
B. It uses multiple lightweight agents for high availability without a single point of failure
C. It can synchronize directly to multiple forests without additional configuration
D. It does not support password hash synchronization
explain: Entra Cloud Sync uses multiple lightweight provisioning agents that can be installed on several servers, providing high availability and eliminating the single point of failure that exists with the traditional Entra Connect sync client. Both solutions support large object counts and PHS.

q: What is the default synchronization interval when using Microsoft Entra Connect to sync changes from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Every 30 minutes
B. Every 60 minutes
C. Every 3 hours
D. Real-time synchronization
explain: The default synchronization cycle for Entra Connect is every 30 minutes. While you can force a sync or change the schedule, the out-of-the-box setting is 30 minutes. Real-time synchronization is not available with Entra Connect.

q: You are the identity administrator for Fabrikam. The company has recently acquired a startup that uses Google Workspace. Fabrikam wants these external users to access internal resources using their Google accounts. What is the recommended approach?
choices: A. Create local accounts for all external users
B. Use Microsoft Entra B2B with Google as an identity provider
C. Configure federation using AD FS
D. Use Microsoft Entra B2C with custom policies
explain: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration natively supports Google as an identity provider, allowing external users to sign in with their Google accounts without creating new credentials. This is the simplest and most secure approach for partner users. B2C is intended for consumer applications, not internal resource access.

q: Which attribute is used by default to match on-premises AD users with Microsoft Entra ID accounts during the synchronization process with Entra Connect?
choices: A. objectGUID
B. userPrincipalName
C. mail
D. msDS-ConsistencyGuid
explain: By default, Entra Connect uses the msDS-ConsistencyGuid attribute (which is populated with the objectGUID value) as the source anchor for matching objects. This provides more flexibility than using objectGUID directly because it can be moved between forests. UPN and mail are used for sign-in but not as the immutable source anchor.

q: A company wants to implement a hybrid identity solution with the least possible on-premises footprint. They need to support password hash synchronization and self-service password reset writeback. Which deployment model meets these requirements?
choices: A. Entra Connect with full SQL Server
B. Entra Cloud Sync
C. Entra Connect with pass-through authentication only
D. AD FS with Entra Connect
explain: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is specifically designed for organizations wanting a minimal on-premises footprint. It runs as a lightweight agent, supports password hash synchronization, and enables password writeback for self-service password reset. It is the strategic future direction from Microsoft.

q: You need to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 resources from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Create a policy with User risk as Medium and above, grant access with MFA
B. Create a policy with Locations set to Any location except trusted locations, grant access requiring MFA
C. Create a policy with Device platforms set to All platforms, grant access requiring MFA
D. Create a policy with Cloud apps set to All cloud apps, block access when sign-in risk is Low
explain: Option B is correct because it specifically targets external access using named locations (trusted locations), which is the standard and most efficient way to require MFA for non-corporate networks. Option A incorrectly uses risk-based conditions instead of location. Option C would require MFA everywhere including inside the office. Option D uses a block action instead of MFA requirement.

q: What is the primary difference between User risk and Sign-in risk detections in Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
choices: A. User risk is calculated in real time while Sign-in risk is calculated offline
B. User risk represents the probability that a user account has been compromised, while Sign-in risk represents the probability that a specific authentication request is compromised
C. Sign-in risk can only be remediated with password reset while User risk can be remediated with MFA
D. User risk applies only to hybrid identities while Sign-in risk applies to cloud-only identities
explain: Option B is correct because User risk focuses on the likelihood an account is compromised (e.g., leaked credentials), whereas Sign-in risk evaluates the specific login attempt (e.g., anomalous location or impossible travel). Option A is incorrect as both can be real-time or offline. Option C is wrong because both can use similar remediation methods. Option D is incorrect as both apply to all identity types.

q: Contoso is piloting passwordless authentication. The security team wants to allow users to sign in with FIDO2 security keys for Microsoft 365 but only from compliant devices. Which two configurations are required? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Enable the FIDO2 security key method in the Authentication methods policy
B. Create a Conditional Access policy requiring compliant device and grant with Passwordless sign-in
C. Configure a custom authentication strength that includes FIDO2
D. Enable passwordless sign-in in the Entra ID tenant settings
explain: Option A is correct because the Authentication methods policy must explicitly enable FIDO2 keys before they can be used. Option C is also correct because authentication strengths allow Conditional Access policies to require specific methods like FIDO2. Option B is incorrect because there is no 'Passwordless sign-in' grant control. Option D is incorrect as there is no such tenant-wide setting.

q: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Only through the MySecurityInfo portal
B. Through the MySecurityInfo portal, during Windows 10/11 OOBE, or via Microsoft Authenticator
C. Only during Windows Hello for Business provisioning
D. Through the Entra admin center under Protection > Authentication methods
explain: Option B is correct because users can register FIDO2 keys via the MySecurityInfo portal, during Windows setup, and through the Authenticator app. Option A is too restrictive. Option C is incorrect because FIDO2 and Windows Hello for Business are separate. Option D is incorrect because end users cannot register keys from the admin center.

q: A user reports they cannot complete MFA registration because they do not have a mobile phone. The organization wants to allow this user to use Microsoft Authenticator on a tablet instead. What should you do?
choices: A. Enable 'Remember MFA on trusted devices' in the MFA service settings
B. Add the tablet's browser as a trusted device in Conditional Access
C. Enable the Microsoft Authenticator app as an available authentication method in the Authentication methods policy
D. Create a Conditional Access policy excluding the user from MFA requirements
explain: Option C is correct because the Authentication methods policy controls which methods (including Authenticator app) are available for users to register and use. Option A only controls persistent sessions. Option B does not enable the method. Option D would weaken security and is not best practice.

q: You are configuring a Conditional Access policy to require MFA for all administrators. The policy should not apply when an administrator is accessing the Entra admin center from a hybrid Azure AD joined device in the corporate office. Which two conditions should you configure? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Include all users, then exclude the Administrators role
B. Include specific users and groups that contain the admin accounts
C. Configure Locations to exclude the corporate office IP ranges
D. Configure Device state to exclude Hybrid Azure AD joined devices
explain: Option B is correct because targeting specific admin groups or roles is the recommended method. Option C is correct because excluding trusted corporate locations prevents MFA when admins are in the office. Option A is wrong because you should not include all users then exclude roles for admin-only policies. Option D is incorrect because excluding hybrid joined devices would likely increase MFA prompts.

q: What is the effect of setting a risk-based Conditional Access policy to 'Medium and above' for Sign-in risk with a 'Block access' control?
choices: A. All users with any sign-in risk will be blocked
B. Users with medium or high sign-in risk will be blocked from signing in
C. Only users with high sign-in risk will be blocked
D. Users will be prompted for MFA instead of being blocked
explain: Option B is correct because selecting 'Medium and above' includes both medium and high risk sign-ins, and the 'Block' grant control prevents access. Option A is incorrect because low risk is excluded. Option C is incorrect because it ignores medium risk. Option D is wrong because the policy uses Block, not Require MFA.

q: Your organization wants to implement phishing-resistant MFA. Which authentication method should you recommend?
choices: A. SMS-based verification code
B. Microsoft Authenticator app push notification
C. FIDO2 security key
D. Voice call verification
explain: Option C is correct because FIDO2 security keys are phishing-resistant as the private key never leaves the device and requires physical presence. Options A, B, and D can all be phished to varying degrees. Microsoft recommends FIDO2 or Windows Hello for Business for phishing-resistant authentication.

q: You notice several users have a 'User risk' state of 'At risk' in the Identity Protection dashboard. What is the recommended first step to remediate these users?
choices: A. Immediately disable all accounts
B. Configure a Conditional Access policy with User risk condition set to Medium and above requiring password change
C. Enable self-remediation by allowing users to change their password using the MyAccount portal
D. Run a risk detection report and investigate each user manually
explain: Option B is correct because a risk-based Conditional Access policy is the recommended automated way to force password changes for users at risk. Option A is too disruptive. Option C is not possible because users at risk are typically blocked from self-service password reset. Option D is manual and not scalable for many users.

q: Which of the following cannot be used as a condition in a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy?
choices: A. User risk level
B. Browser type and version
C. Client app type (Exchange ActiveSync, Browser, etc.)
D. Number of days since last password change
explain: Option D is correct because Conditional Access does not support 'days since last password change' as a condition. Options A, B, and C are all valid conditions: User risk is available when Identity Protection is enabled, browser can be filtered, and client app type is a standard condition.

q: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 resources from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Create a policy with Users: All users, Cloud apps: Microsoft 365, Conditions: Location (Any location except trusted locations), Grant: Require MFA
B. Create a policy with Users: All users, Cloud apps: All cloud apps, Conditions: Device platforms: All devices, Grant: Require MFA
C. Create a policy with Users: All guest users, Cloud apps: Office 365, Conditions: Client apps: Mobile apps and desktop clients, Grant: Require MFA
D. Create a policy with Users: All users, Cloud apps: Microsoft 365, Conditions: Sign-in risk: Medium and above, Grant: Require MFA
explain: Option A is correct because it specifically targets external access using named locations (trusted locations) and applies only to Microsoft 365 apps, which is the most targeted and least disruptive approach. Option B is too broad as it would require MFA from inside the corporate network as well. Option C only targets guests and specific client apps, which does not meet the requirement. Option D relies on Identity Protection risk signals instead of location, which is not the requirement.

q: What is the primary difference between Security defaults and Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Security defaults cannot be customized while Conditional Access policies are fully customizable
B. Security defaults only apply to Azure AD Premium P1 while Conditional Access requires P2
C. Security defaults protect only against password spray while Conditional Access protects against all attacks
D. Security defaults require a minimum of 10 users while Conditional Access has no user limit
explain: Security defaults provide a basic set of preconfigured security settings that cannot be modified, whereas Conditional Access policies offer granular, customizable control over when and how authentication is enforced. Both features are available with Azure AD Premium P1. Security defaults enable multiple security features including MFA for all users.

q: Your organization is piloting passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. A pilot user reports they can no longer sign in after their phone was replaced. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A. The user must re-register the new device in the Authentication methods blade
B. The Conditional Access policy is blocking the new device
C. The user's password has expired
D. The user needs to contact the help desk to reset their password hash
explain: Passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator is tied to the specific device. When a user gets a new phone, they must re-register the new device as an authentication method. This is a common scenario during passwordless deployments. Options B, C, and D are not the primary cause of this specific issue.

q: Which of the following correctly describes how Microsoft Entra ID Identity Protection risk detections work?
choices: A. Sign-in risk evaluates the likelihood that the sign-in was performed by the identity owner, while user risk evaluates the likelihood that the user account has been compromised
B. User risk only evaluates anonymous IP addresses while sign-in risk evaluates all risk types
C. Both user risk and sign-in risk require Azure AD Premium P2 and cannot be used with Conditional Access
D. Identity Protection risk detections only work with on-premises Active Directory accounts
explain: Identity Protection uses two main risk types: user risk (likelihood the account is compromised) and sign-in risk (likelihood the sign-in request is not from the account owner). These risk signals can be used in Conditional Access policies and are available with Microsoft Entra ID P2. Option C is incorrect because risk-based policies are commonly used with Conditional Access.

q: You need to implement MFA for a group of executives who frequently travel internationally. The solution must minimize false positives while still providing strong security. Which Conditional Access configuration should you use?
choices: A. Require MFA for all sign-ins from locations outside the corporate HQ
B. Require MFA when sign-in risk is detected as medium or high
C. Require MFA for all sign-ins regardless of location or risk
D. Block access from any country outside of the executives' normal travel regions
explain: Using sign-in risk as a condition (option B) is the most intelligent approach as it leverages Identity Protection's machine learning to only challenge users when anomalous behavior is detected. This reduces friction for legitimate travel while still providing strong protection. Option A would create excessive MFA prompts during normal travel. Option C creates too much friction. Option D could inadvertently block legitimate travel.

q: What is the minimum license required to use risk-based Conditional Access policies that leverage Identity Protection?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra ID Free
B. Microsoft Entra ID P1
C. Microsoft Entra ID P2
D. Microsoft 365 E3
explain: Risk-based Conditional Access policies that use user risk and sign-in risk require Microsoft Entra ID P2 (formerly Azure AD Premium P2). Microsoft Entra ID P1 includes Conditional Access but not the Identity Protection risk analytics. Microsoft 365 E3 includes P1 capabilities but not P2.

q: Contoso is implementing phishing-resistant authentication. The security team wants to require Windows Hello for Business for all users accessing sensitive applications. Which policy type should be used to enforce this requirement?
choices: A. Authentication strength Conditional Access policy
B. Named location policy
C. Identity Protection user risk policy
D. Authentication methods policy in the MFA blade
explain: Authentication strength policies (a type of Conditional Access grant control) allow organizations to require specific strong authentication methods such as phishing-resistant methods like Windows Hello for Business or FIDO2 keys. This is the recommended modern approach for enforcing phishing-resistant authentication. The other options cannot enforce specific authentication methods at this granularity.

q: A user receives a Conditional Access prompt requiring MFA but their only registered authentication method is a phone number that no longer works. What is the recommended administrative action?
choices: A. Use the Authentication methods blade to add a temporary access pass for the user
B. Disable the Conditional Access policy for this user
C. Reset the user's password from the Microsoft Entra admin center
D. Delete and recreate the user account
explain: A Temporary Access Pass (TAP) is the recommended secure method to allow a user to sign in and register new MFA methods when they have lost access to all their authentication methods. Option B would weaken security. Password reset (option C) would not help if they cannot complete MFA. Option D is unnecessary and disruptive.

q: Which of the following is a valid authentication method that can be used with passwordless sign-in in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. FIDO2 security key
B. SMS-based one-time passcode
C. Security questions
D. Email-based OTP
explain: FIDO2 security keys are fully supported for passwordless sign-in and are phishing-resistant. SMS, security questions, and email OTP are not considered passwordless methods and do not meet modern passwordless requirements. Microsoft strongly recommends FIDO2 keys or Microsoft Authenticator for passwordless scenarios.

q: You are investigating a risky user flagged by Identity Protection. The user risk level is listed as High and the detection type is 'Leaked credentials'. What is the recommended immediate action?
choices: A. Force the user to change their password on next sign-in and reset their MFA methods
B. Monitor the account for the next 24 hours before taking action
C. Disable the user's account permanently
D. Add the user to an exclusion list for Identity Protection
explain: When Identity Protection detects leaked credentials with a High risk level, the recommended action is to force a password change and re-register MFA methods. This mitigates the immediate risk of the compromised credentials being used. Simply monitoring (B) or permanently disabling (C) are not the best first responses. Excluding the user (D) would reduce security.

q: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 apps from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Create a policy with Users: All users, Cloud apps: Microsoft 365, Conditions: Location (exclude trusted IPs), Grant: Require MFA
B. Create a policy with Users: All users, Cloud apps: All cloud apps, Conditions: Device state (include hybrid Azure AD joined), Grant: Require MFA
C. Enable Security defaults in Microsoft Entra ID
D. Create a named location for the corporate network and apply it to the MFA registration policy
explain: Option A is correct because it specifically targets access from outside trusted locations for Microsoft 365 apps, meeting the requirement with precision. Option B incorrectly uses device state instead of location. Security defaults (C) would enforce broader MFA requirements that may exceed the stated need. Option D only handles registration, not enforcement during sign-in.

q: What is the primary difference between User Risk and Sign-in Risk detections in Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
choices: A. User Risk is calculated in real time while Sign-in Risk is calculated offline
B. User Risk focuses on the probability that a user account has been compromised, while Sign-in Risk focuses on the probability that a specific authentication request is compromised
C. Sign-in Risk can only trigger block actions while User Risk can only trigger MFA
D. User Risk requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 while Sign-in Risk works with P1
explain: Option B is correct. User Risk assesses the likelihood an identity has been compromised (e.g., leaked credentials), whereas Sign-in Risk evaluates the legitimacy of a particular login attempt (e.g., anomalous location or impossible travel). The other options contain factual inaccuracies regarding timing, available controls, and licensing.

q: Contoso recently enabled passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. Some users report they can no longer sign in from their iOS devices. Which setting should you verify first?
choices: A. Ensure the Authentication methods policy has 'Microsoft Authenticator' enabled for passwordless sign-in
B. Verify that Conditional Access policies do not block the 'Authenticator App' client app
C. Check that users have registered FIDO2 security keys as a fallback method
D. Confirm that iOS devices are marked as compliant in Intune
explain: Option A is correct because the Authentication methods policy must explicitly enable passwordless phone sign-in for the Microsoft Authenticator app. The other choices, while potentially relevant in other scenarios, are not the primary reason passwordless sign-in would fail specifically on iOS devices after enabling the feature.

q: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Only through the My Security Info portal when the user is already signed in
B. Through the My Security Info portal or during Windows 10/11 out-of-box experience (OOBE) when joined to Microsoft Entra ID
C. Only by an administrator using the Microsoft Entra admin center
D. Through the Microsoft Authenticator app on mobile devices
explain: Option B is correct. FIDO2 keys can be registered by users via My Security Info or during the OOBE for Microsoft Entra joined devices. Option A is too restrictive, C is incorrect because users can self-register, and D is false because the Authenticator app does not register FIDO2 keys.

q: You need to reduce the risk of MFA fatigue attacks against executives. Which Conditional Access policy setting should you configure?
choices: A. Sign-in risk as Low and above with a grant control of Require password change
B. Configure an authentication strength requiring phishing-resistant methods for the executive group
C. Block legacy authentication protocols for all users
D. Require compliant device for all cloud apps
explain: Option B is correct because requiring phishing-resistant authentication methods (such as FIDO2 or Windows Hello for Business) significantly mitigates MFA fatigue (also known as push bombing) attacks. The other options do not directly address the MFA fatigue vector.

q: What occurs when a user is added to the 'Users at high risk' risk-based Conditional Access policy with a 'Block access' grant control?
choices: A. The user is immediately blocked from all sign-ins until an admin resets the password
B. The user is blocked only when Microsoft Entra ID Protection calculates a high user risk level
C. The policy has no effect until the user attempts to register for MFA
D. The user receives a warning but can still sign in from trusted locations
explain: Option B is correct. Risk-based policies evaluate the risk level calculated by Identity Protection at the time of sign-in. If the user's risk is high, the block is enforced. Option A is incorrect because blocking is risk-based, not permanent. Options C and D misrepresent the policy behavior.

q: Your organization wants to implement number matching in Microsoft Authenticator to improve MFA security. Which license is required to use this feature?
choices: A. Microsoft Entra ID Free
B. Microsoft Entra ID P1
C. Microsoft Entra ID P2
D. Microsoft 365 E3
explain: Option C is correct. Number matching and additional advanced MFA features such as location context in the Authenticator app require Microsoft Entra ID P2 licensing. P1 and Free tiers do not support these enhanced MFA protections.

q: You notice several users have been flagged for 'Anonymous IP address' sign-in risk. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A. Users are signing in from a TOR network
B. Users have outdated operating systems
C. The users' passwords have been leaked on the dark web
D. Users are signing in from a new country
explain: Option A is correct. The 'Anonymous IP address' detection typically indicates sign-ins from anonymous proxy services such as TOR. Option C relates to leaked credentials (User Risk), while B and D relate to other risk detections such as unfamiliar features or atypical travel.

q: Which of the following best describes the effect of enabling 'Require reauthentication every 30 days' in a Conditional Access policy for Microsoft 365 applications?
choices: A. Users must re-enter their password and complete MFA every 30 days
B. Users are forced to register a new MFA method every 30 days
C. The policy has no effect because sign-in frequency is configured in the Authentication methods policy
D. Users must perform MFA every time they access the application after 30 days of inactivity
explain: Option A is correct. The Sign-in frequency control in Conditional Access can require users to reauthenticate (password + MFA) at a specified interval. Option D is close but incorrect because the control applies regardless of activity. The other options are factually wrong.

q: A security audit reveals that several service accounts are using basic authentication to access Exchange Online. What is the recommended approach to secure these accounts while maintaining functionality?
choices: A. Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks legacy authentication for all users except the service accounts
B. Enable modern authentication on the service accounts and update the applications to use OAuth 2.0 with a client secret or certificate
C. Add the service accounts to the break-glass emergency access group
D. Register the service accounts for MFA using a hardware token
explain: Option B is correct. The long-term recommended solution is to move away from basic authentication entirely by adopting modern authentication with OAuth 2.0 using secrets or certificates. Blocking legacy auth (A) would break the service accounts. Options C and D do not solve the root problem.

q: Your organization needs to allow a third-party SaaS application to authenticate users via single sign-on without storing credentials. The solution must support both SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Which workload identity type should you create in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Managed identity
B. Enterprise application only
C. App registration
D. Service principal without app registration
explain: An app registration is required when you need to configure custom authentication settings, expose APIs, or support modern protocols such as OIDC and SAML for third-party applications. Enterprise applications represent the instantiated service principal but do not allow you to configure authentication flows or certificates. Managed identities are designed for Azure resource-to-Azure resource authentication and do not support SAML/OIDC federation with SaaS apps.

q: Contoso is implementing single sign-on for an on-premises web application that supports SAML 2.0. The application must be registered in Microsoft Entra ID. What is the correct object to create first?
choices: A. A managed identity assigned to the web server
B. An app registration with Redirect URI
C. An enterprise application using the Non-gallery option
D. A system-assigned managed identity
explain: For SAML-based SSO with non-gallery applications, you create an enterprise application directly from the Microsoft Entra admin center using the Non-gallery option. This automatically creates the associated service principal. An app registration is not required for simple SAML enterprise apps. Managed identities cannot be used for SAML federation with on-premises web apps.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding the difference between an app registration and an enterprise application in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. An app registration is the local representation; the enterprise application is the global representation
B. An app registration defines the application in the tenant; the enterprise application is the service principal instance
C. An enterprise application can be used for OIDC but an app registration cannot
D. Only enterprise applications can be granted API permissions
explain: An app registration is the definition of the application within the tenant (where you configure API permissions, authentication, and branding). The enterprise application is the service principal object that represents the instantiated application in the directory. Both can be used for OIDC and SAML. API permissions are requested on the app registration.

q: You need to enable a logic app to authenticate to Microsoft Graph using its own identity without storing any credentials. What should you configure?
choices: A. App registration with client secret
B. User-assigned managed identity
C. Enterprise application with SAML SSO
D. System-assigned managed identity on the Logic App
explain: A system-assigned managed identity is automatically created and tied to the lifecycle of the Logic App. It can obtain tokens for Microsoft Graph without any credential management. User-assigned managed identities are standalone and reusable across resources. App registrations require secret or certificate management, which violates the no-credential requirement.

q: Your company wants to implement SSO for a custom line-of-business application using OpenID Connect. The application will run in Azure Container Apps. What is the recommended identity approach?
choices: A. Register the app in Microsoft Entra ID, then use a user-assigned managed identity for the container
B. Create an app registration, configure OIDC settings, and use client credentials flow with a certificate
C. Create only an enterprise application with OIDC enabled
D. Use a system-assigned managed identity and configure it as a SAML provider
explain: For a custom application using OIDC, you must create an app registration to configure the authentication settings, redirect URIs, and expose the application as a relying party. A certificate should be used instead of a client secret for production workloads. Managed identities are not used as the identity of the application itself when the app needs to act as an OIDC client; they are better suited for Azure resource authentication.

q: What is the maximum number of credentials (secrets or certificates) that can be added to a single app registration in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: D. Unlimited
explain: Microsoft Entra ID supports a maximum of 50 credentials (combination of client secrets and certificates) per app registration. This limit helps prevent abuse while still allowing rotation strategies. The other numbers listed are incorrect.

q: You are planning workload identities for several Azure Functions that need to call Azure Key Vault. The solution must follow least privilege and support automatic credential rotation. Which identity type meets these requirements?
choices: A. App registration with client secret rotated every 30 days
B. System-assigned managed identity with RBAC role assignment
C. Enterprise application using password-based SSO
D. User-assigned managed identity with a manually uploaded certificate
explain: System-assigned managed identities provide Azure AD-backed identities that require no credential management and support automatic rotation. They are the Microsoft-recommended approach for Azure Functions accessing Key Vault. App registrations require secret or certificate management. Enterprise applications with password SSO are not suitable for service-to-service scenarios.

q: A developer has created an app registration for a daemon application that uses the client credentials flow. The application must be restricted so it can only obtain tokens for the Microsoft Graph API permission User.Read.All. Where should you configure this restriction?
choices: A. In the enterprise application blade under Permissions
B. In the app registration under API permissions and then grant admin consent
C. In the app registration under Authentication settings
D. In Conditional Access policies only
explain: API permissions are configured on the app registration object. After adding the delegated or application permission (User.Read.All in this case), admin consent must be granted. The enterprise application blade shows the granted permissions but you cannot add them there. Authentication settings control sign-in methods, not permission scoping.

q: Your security team requires that all workload identities use certificate-based authentication instead of client secrets. Which two objects can be configured to support certificate credentials? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Managed identity
B. App registration
C. Enterprise application
D. System-assigned identity for an Azure VM
explain: Only app registrations (and the associated service principals) support the upload of X.509 certificates for authentication. Managed identities (both system-assigned and user-assigned) use Azure AD-issued tokens and do not support or require certificates. Enterprise applications are the service principal instances and inherit the credential capability from the app registration.

q: You need to enable SAML-based SSO for a gallery application that appears in the Microsoft Entra application gallery. What is the simplest method?
choices: A. Create a new app registration and manually configure SAML settings
B. Add the application from the gallery as an enterprise application and configure SSO
C. Assign a managed identity to the application
D. Create both an app registration and an enterprise application manually
explain: Gallery applications are pre-integrated and should be added as enterprise applications directly from the gallery. This automatically provisions the correct SAML configuration templates and best practices. Creating a separate app registration is unnecessary and can cause duplication. Managed identities are not used for SAML SSO to gallery SaaS applications.

q: Your organization needs to allow a third-party SaaS application to access Microsoft Graph data on behalf of users without storing credentials. Which workload identity type should you use, and which protocol is most appropriate?
choices: A. Enterprise application with SAML
B. App registration with a client secret and OAuth 2.0
C. Managed identity with OIDC
D. App registration with a certificate and SAML
explain: An app registration with a client secret (or certificate) combined with the OAuth 2.0 authorization code or client credentials flow is the correct approach for a third-party SaaS app to securely call Microsoft Graph. SAML is used for web SSO, not API access. Managed identities are for Azure resources only and do not support third-party SaaS scenarios in this context. Enterprise applications are the instantiated service principals, not the registration itself.

q: You are planning to implement single sign-on for a custom line-of-business application that supports OpenID Connect. The application must request both an ID token and an access token. Which two objects must you create in Microsoft Entra ID? (Choose two.)
choices: A. An enterprise application only
B. An app registration and an enterprise application
C. A managed identity and a service principal
D. An app registration and a conditional access policy
explain: You must create an app registration to define the application’s identity, redirect URIs, API permissions, and token configuration. An enterprise application (service principal) is automatically created in the tenant when you register the app and is required for SSO and assignment. Managed identities are for Azure resources only. A conditional access policy is optional for additional controls.

q: Contoso wants to enable SSO for an on-premises application that only supports SAML 2.0. The application will be accessed by users in multiple Azure AD tenants. What is the recommended approach?
choices: A. Create a multitenant app registration and configure SAML SSO on the enterprise application
B. Use a system-assigned managed identity with SAML
C. Create a single-tenant app registration and use OIDC
D. Register the application as an enterprise app only without an app registration
explain: For SAML-based SSO with external tenants, a multitenant app registration is required so each tenant can consent and create its own service principal. The SAML SSO settings are then configured on the enterprise application object. Managed identities cannot be used for SAML SSO. OIDC is not supported by the application. An enterprise app cannot exist without a corresponding app registration for custom SAML apps.

q: Which of the following is true regarding managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. They can be used to authenticate to on-premises applications using SAML
B. They automatically rotate their credentials and can be granted permissions to Azure resources without storing secrets
C. They require manual certificate management and are visible in the App registrations blade
D. They can only be used with user-assigned identities for outbound API calls
explain: Managed identities (both system-assigned and user-assigned) eliminate the need to store credentials because Entra ID automatically handles credential rotation. They are commonly used to authenticate to Azure resources via Microsoft Entra ID. They do not support SAML for on-premises apps, are not visible under App registrations, and do not require manual certificate management.

q: You need to grant a web application the ability to call the Microsoft Graph API as the signed-in user. The application uses OIDC for authentication. What should you configure on the app registration?
choices: A. Add delegated permissions for Microsoft Graph and use the authorization code flow
B. Add application permissions and use the client credentials flow
C. Enable implicit grant flow for access tokens
D. Configure a SAML signing certificate
explain: To act on behalf of the signed-in user, you must request delegated permissions and use the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (with PKCE for public clients). Application permissions and client credentials flow run as the application itself, not the user. Implicit grant is considered legacy. SAML is not used with Microsoft Graph API calls.

q: A company is migrating several enterprise applications from ADFS to Microsoft Entra ID. Many of the applications were configured with relying party trusts using WS-Federation. What is the recommended replacement protocol when moving to Entra ID?
choices: A. Continue using WS-Federation
B. Use SAML 2.0
C. Switch to OIDC
D. Use OAuth 2.0 client credentials
explain: Microsoft Entra ID primarily supports SAML 2.0 for enterprise applications that previously used WS-Federation in ADFS. While OIDC is preferred for modern applications, legacy enterprise apps that only support WS-Fed/SAML should be configured with SAML 2.0 in Entra ID. WS-Federation is not natively supported for new configurations in Entra ID.

q: You have an Azure Function that needs to read secrets from Azure Key Vault without storing any credentials in code or configuration. Which workload identity type meets this requirement with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. App registration with a client secret
B. System-assigned managed identity
C. Enterprise application with SAML SSO
D. User-assigned managed identity only
explain: A system-assigned managed identity is automatically created with the Azure Function, automatically receives a service principal, and Entra ID rotates its credentials. You simply grant the managed identity the required Key Vault RBAC or access policy. App registrations require secret/certificate management. SAML is irrelevant for this scenario.

q: What is the key difference between an app registration and an enterprise application in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. App registrations define the application’s configuration across tenants; enterprise applications are tenant-specific instances
B. Enterprise applications are used only for SAML; app registrations are used only for OIDC
C. App registrations cannot be granted API permissions
D. Enterprise applications are created first and automatically create app registrations
explain: The app registration (application object) lives in the home tenant and defines global settings such as branding, redirect URIs, and API permissions. The enterprise application (service principal) is the tenant-specific instance that holds assignments, SSO settings, and user consent. The other options are incorrect statements.

q: Your security team requires that all workload identities use certificate-based authentication instead of client secrets. Which two methods allow you to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Upload a certificate to an app registration
B. Use a system-assigned managed identity
C. Configure a federated identity credential with GitHub
D. Add a client secret with a very long expiration
explain: Uploading an X.509 certificate to an app registration is a supported method for certificate-based authentication. Federated identity credentials (workload identity federation) also remove the need for secrets by using external identity providers. Managed identities use their own automatic credential system but are not configured via certificates on app registrations. Long-lived client secrets are explicitly against the requirement.

q: You are configuring SSO for a new SaaS application that supports OIDC and is listed in the Microsoft Entra gallery. What is the simplest way to add and configure this application?
choices: A. Create a new app registration manually and then create an enterprise application
B. Add the application from the Entra gallery; an enterprise application is created automatically
C. Create a managed identity and link it to the SaaS application
D. Register the application as multitenant and configure SAML manually
explain: Gallery applications automatically create the enterprise application (service principal) and pre-populate SSO settings when added from the Entra gallery. This is the simplest and recommended method. Manual app registration is unnecessary for gallery apps. Managed identities cannot be used for SaaS SSO. The application uses OIDC, not SAML.

q: Your organization needs to allow a third-party SaaS application to access Microsoft Graph data on behalf of users without storing credentials. The application must support single sign-on. Which authentication protocol should you configure when registering the app in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. SAML 2.0
B. OAuth 2.0 with OpenID Connect
C. WS-Federation
D. LDAP
explain: OAuth 2.0 with OpenID Connect is the correct choice because it enables delegated access to Microsoft Graph using modern authentication flows and supports SSO. SAML is primarily used for enterprise SSO to web apps, not for calling Microsoft Graph APIs on behalf of users. WS-Federation and LDAP are legacy protocols not suitable for this scenario.

q: You are planning to implement a managed identity for an Azure Function that needs to authenticate to Azure Key Vault. Which type of managed identity should you use if the function will be deployed to multiple regions and must continue to work if one region fails?
choices: A. System-assigned managed identity
B. User-assigned managed identity
C. Hybrid managed identity
D. On-premises managed identity
explain: A user-assigned managed identity is the correct choice because it is a standalone Azure resource that can be assigned to multiple instances across regions. System-assigned identities are tied to the lifecycle of a single resource and would not survive region failover as easily. The other options do not exist in Microsoft Entra ID.

q: Which of the following is true regarding the difference between app registrations and enterprise applications in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. App registrations define the application in the tenant where it was created; enterprise applications are the service principal instances in each tenant where the app is used.
B. Enterprise applications are used only for SAML SSO, while app registrations are used only for OIDC.
C. App registrations cannot be granted API permissions; only enterprise applications can.
D. There is no functional difference between the two objects.
explain: App registrations represent the application definition (client ID, secrets, permissions) in the home tenant, while enterprise applications are the service principal objects that represent instances of that app in each tenant. Option B is incorrect because both can support multiple protocols. Option C is wrong because permissions are requested in the app registration.

q: Contoso is implementing SSO for a new line-of-business web application using SAML 2.0. The application requires the user’s email address and department to be sent in the SAML assertion. Where should you configure the required claims?
choices: A. In the app registration blade under API permissions
B. In the enterprise application blade under Single sign-on > Attributes & Claims
C. In Microsoft Entra ID > User settings
D. In the application’s own configuration file only
explain: Claims for SAML-based enterprise applications are configured in the enterprise application’s Single sign-on section under Attributes & Claims. App registrations handle OAuth/OIDC scopes and claims differently. User settings and the application config alone cannot control what Entra ID sends in the SAML token.

q: You need to grant an Azure Logic App the ability to read secrets from Azure Key Vault without using client secrets or certificates. What is the recommended and most secure approach?
choices: A. Register an app and upload a certificate
B. Use a system-assigned managed identity and assign Key Vault permissions
C. Use a service principal with a client secret rotated every 30 days
D. Enable Azure AD Domain Services
explain: Using a system-assigned managed identity is the recommended approach because Microsoft Entra ID automatically manages the identity lifecycle and no secrets are stored. Certificates and client secrets introduce secret management overhead. Azure AD Domain Services is unrelated to workload identities.

q: What is the maximum validity period you can configure for a client secret created on an app registration in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. 6 months
B. 12 months
C. 24 months
D. 36 months
explain: Microsoft Entra ID allows client secrets to be valid for up to 24 months (2 years). While shorter periods are recommended for security, the platform maximum is 24 months. The other values are either too short or exceed the current platform limit.

q: Your company’s security policy requires that all workload identities use certificate-based authentication instead of client secrets. When creating an app registration, where do you upload the certificate?
choices: A. Under Certificates & secrets > Certificates
B. Under API permissions
C. Under Branding
D. Under Owners
explain: Certificates are uploaded in the Certificates & secrets blade under the Certificates tab. This enables the application to authenticate using the certificate instead of a secret. The other sections do not support certificate upload for authentication.

q: You have an on-premises application that needs to authenticate to Microsoft 365 using modern authentication. The application cannot use a browser redirect. Which OAuth 2.0 flow should be implemented?
choices: A. Authorization code flow
B. Implicit flow
C. Client credentials flow
D. Device authorization grant flow
explain: The device authorization grant flow (device code flow) is designed for devices or applications that cannot display a browser. It allows the user to visit a URL on another device to sign in. Client credentials flow is for daemon apps without user context. Authorization code and implicit flows require browser interaction.

q: Which Microsoft Entra ID feature allows you to restrict which users and groups can sign in to a specific enterprise application that uses SAML SSO?
choices: A. Conditional Access policies assigned to the enterprise app
B. App registration manifest settings
C. Azure AD Connect sync rules
D. Application proxy settings
explain: Conditional Access policies can be scoped directly to enterprise applications to control user access. The app registration manifest does not control user assignment. Sync rules and Application Proxy are for different purposes.

q: You are designing a workload identity strategy for several Azure resources that need to authenticate to each other. Microsoft recommends using managed identities instead of service principals with client secrets for this purpose. Why?
choices: A. Managed identities automatically rotate credentials and eliminate secret management.
B. Managed identities cost less than service principals.
C. Service principals cannot be granted RBAC permissions.
D. Managed identities support SAML but service principals do not.
explain: Managed identities eliminate the need to store and rotate credentials because Microsoft Entra ID handles authentication completely. This significantly reduces administrative overhead and security risk. The other statements are false: both can use RBAC, cost is not the primary factor, and SAML is not the relevant protocol for service-to-service communication.

q: Your organization wants to automatically grant access to a set of resources for new contractors for exactly 90 days. Which Microsoft Entra ID feature should you use to meet this requirement with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Entitlement management access packages
B. Privileged Identity Management (PIM) eligible assignments
C. Access reviews
D. Lifecycle workflows
explain: Entitlement management access packages allow you to bundle resources with defined policies including automatic expiration after a set number of days. PIM is for privileged roles only and does not provide automatic time-bound package assignment for general resources. Access reviews are for periodic attestation, not automated provisioning. Lifecycle workflows focus on joiner/mover/leaver scenarios rather than time-bound entitlement packages.

q: You need to ensure that all users who are members of the 'Finance-Approvers' group have their group membership reviewed every 90 days. What should you create in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. An access package with a policy requiring approval
B. A scheduled access review for the group
C. A PIM just-in-time activation policy
D. A lifecycle workflow with a custom task
explain: Access reviews are specifically designed to periodically review and attest to group memberships or access. Access packages focus on requesting and assigning access, not recurring reviews. PIM is for privileged roles and does not replace group membership reviews. Lifecycle workflows are for identity lifecycle events such as onboarding or offboarding, not recurring attestation.

q: What is the primary purpose of using lifecycle workflows in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. To provide just-in-time privileged access to roles
B. To automate identity management tasks during joiner, mover, and leaver events
C. To create access packages for resource entitlement
D. To perform real-time access certification of users
explain: Lifecycle workflows automate tasks such as user provisioning, attribute updates, and offboarding based on HR-driven events. PIM provides just-in-time privileged access. Entitlement management uses access packages. Access reviews focus on certification, not automation of lifecycle events.

q: A company wants to allow users to request membership to an access package that automatically expires after 30 days unless renewed. Which two features must be configured together to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Entitlement management access package with expiration policy
B. Privileged Identity Management activation requirement
C. Access review with self-review enabled
D. Lifecycle workflow with expiration task
explain: Entitlement management access packages support policies that define expiration after a fixed number of days and allow renewal requests. PIM is limited to privileged roles and does not manage general access packages. Access reviews are for attestation, not automatic expiration. Lifecycle workflows do not replace the built-in expiration capabilities of access packages.

q: You are configuring Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for the Global Administrator role. You want to require approval before activation and enforce a maximum activation time of 4 hours. Where do you configure these settings?
choices: A. In an access package policy
B. In a PIM role setting policy
C. In an access review configuration
D. In a lifecycle workflow template
explain: PIM role setting policies allow administrators to require approval, set maximum activation duration, and configure other just-in-time controls for specific roles. Access packages, access reviews, and lifecycle workflows do not control PIM role activation settings.
objective: Plan and implement Privileged Identity Management

q: Your security team requires that all users with the Application Administrator role must justify their continued need for the role every month. Which solution should you implement?
choices: A. Create a recurring access review for the role
B. Configure an access package with mandatory approval
C. Enable PIM with permanent assignments
D. Create a lifecycle workflow that runs monthly
explain: Access reviews can be scheduled to run against privileged roles and require users or managers to attest to continued need. Access packages are for requesting access, not reviewing existing role membership. PIM permanent assignments do not enforce periodic justification. Lifecycle workflows are not designed for recurring role justification.

q: What is the recommended way to automatically remove a user's access to all resources when their employment status changes to 'Terminated' in your HR system?
choices: A. Create a custom script using Microsoft Graph
B. Configure a lifecycle workflow with a 'Leaver' template
C. Schedule a monthly access review for all users
D. Use entitlement management with an expiration policy
explain: Lifecycle workflows include pre-built Leaver templates that automatically revoke access, remove group memberships, and perform other offboarding tasks when triggered by HR attribute changes. Manual scripts require ongoing maintenance. Access reviews and entitlement management expiration are not event-driven by HR status changes.

q: You need to allow users to request temporary access to a SharePoint site and a specific application for a maximum of 14 days. The request must go through a designated approver. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you use?
choices: A. Privileged Identity Management for groups
B. Entitlement management access package
C. Lifecycle workflow with approval task
D. Access review with self-attestation
explain: Entitlement management access packages let you bundle resources (SharePoint site + enterprise application), define request workflows with approvers, and set maximum duration. PIM for groups is limited to security and Microsoft 365 groups for PIM-enabled scenarios. Lifecycle workflows are for automated lifecycle events, not user-driven requests. Access reviews are for review, not initial access requests.

q: Which of the following is a valid use case for using access reviews in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A. Automatically provisioning new users from an HR system
B. Periodically recertifying guest user access to resources
C. Enforcing just-in-time activation of privileged roles
D. Creating time-bound access packages
explain: Access reviews are designed to periodically recertify whether users (especially guests) should continue to have access. Provisioning is handled by lifecycle workflows or HR integration. Just-in-time activation is a PIM feature. Time-bound access is configured within entitlement management access packages.

q: Your organization is implementing Microsoft Entra Permissions Management as part of their identity governance strategy. You want to reduce standing access to highly privileged Azure resources. Which approach aligns best with governance best practices?
choices: A. Assign permanent Owner roles at the subscription level
B. Use PIM with eligible assignments and require justification and approval
C. Create access packages that never expire
D. Disable access reviews for administrative roles
explain: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) with eligible assignments follows the principle of least privilege and zero standing access by requiring activation with justification and approval. Permanent assignments violate governance best practices. Access packages are not typically used for Azure resource roles at scale. Disabling access reviews reduces visibility and control.
objective: Plan and implement Privileged Identity Management

q: You need to automatically grant access to a set of SaaS applications for users in the Marketing department when they are hired, and remove access 30 days after their employment ends. Which Microsoft Entra ID feature should you use to meet this requirement with the least administrative effort?
choices: A. Entitlement management access packages with catalog and policies
B. Privileged Identity Management (PIM) eligible assignments
C. Access reviews with recurring schedule
D. Microsoft Entra Lifecycle Workflows with custom tasks
explain: Microsoft Entra Lifecycle Workflows are designed for joiner-mover-leaver scenarios and can automatically trigger tasks such as granting or revoking access based on employee lifecycle events. Entitlement management is better suited for on-demand access packages, PIM is for privileged roles, and access reviews are for periodic attestation rather than automated lifecycle events.

q: Which of the following is a valid use case for Microsoft Entra Entitlement Management?
choices: A. Automatically elevating users to Global Administrator on a just-in-time basis
B. Creating access packages that allow users to request access to resources with approval workflows
C. Running quarterly reviews of group membership for all security groups
D. Automatically provisioning users into on-premises Active Directory
explain: Entitlement management enables the creation of access packages that bundle resources with built-in request, approval, and lifecycle policies. PIM is used for just-in-time privileged access, access reviews handle attestation, and lifecycle workflows or provisioning handle user lifecycle automation.

q: Your organization wants to require that all users with the Application Administrator role must use Privileged Identity Management to activate the role for a maximum of 4 hours. What should you configure?
choices: A. An access review for the role
B. A PIM role setting with activation maximum duration and require justification
C. An entitlement management access package for the role
D. A lifecycle workflow that assigns the role permanently
explain: PIM role settings allow administrators to define activation duration, require justification, MFA, and approval. Access reviews are for reviewing existing assignments, entitlement management is for packages of resources, and lifecycle workflows are not used to manage privileged role activation.

q: You are planning an access review for all guest users in the organization. The review should occur every quarter, and reviewers should be the guests' sponsors. Which two settings must be configured? (Choose two.)
choices: A. Set review frequency to Quarterly
B. Select Self-review as the reviewer
C. Enable the 'Require reviewers to provide a reason' option
D. Set reviewers to 'Guest's sponsor (User attribute)'
